summary: 20-foot L-4 tower built 1940 south of Cave Junction; dismantled 1980 and its cab moved to Little Grayback Mountain in 1981. No source describes Waldo Hill today.

facts.status_note: Tower dismantled in 1980; its cab was moved to Little Grayback Mountain in 1981 and is still in use there

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com name the Oregon Department of Forestry; the Forest Lookouts page header lists the Siskiyou National Forest before the state. The record's agency is kept as ODF, and the story notes the header.

Forest Lookouts says the tower was dismantled in 1980 while the register and NHLR date the cab's move to 1981. These can both be true: the tower came down in 1980 and the cab was placed at Little Grayback in 1981.
The register and NHLR say the cab was moved; the Little Grayback page and the 2020 blog say much of the material was reused. The story gives both accounts.

The Little Grayback page calls the source the old Waldo Mountain lookout; the 2020 blog says Waldo Hill and warns against confusing it with Waldo Mountain east of Eugene. The Waldo Hill identification is the better supported reading, and the story no longer calls the Little Grayback page's name a slip.

sources.title: Little Grayback – Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains at the Waldo Hill site, or whether it is public. The Little Grayback cab is an active fire-detection and camera site with a surveillance sign, so the story gives no visit advice. The NHLR listing for Little Grayback gives a 1971 build date, while the 1980 annual report and the 2020 blog date construction to 1980-81; the story follows the latter, and the NHLR date is worth a check. The 2020 blog is a personal visit report, not an official source. The geocache page cited on the Waldo register page returned no text and was not used. Access fields are omitted for Waldo Hill because they describe the gone site, which no source covers. The county name was removed from the summary because no cited source names it.
